title: Dedicated elasticity SLA lexicon and error-budget playbook
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create canonical SLA definitions, error-budget computation method, and contract-ready remediation language for Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU) customers that need elastic throughput guarantees. This ticket consolidates measurement windows, metric lexicon, credit formulas, incident notification rules, and autoscale/fleet controls constraints into a single playbook suitable for legal/finance, sales negotiation, and engineering implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A single, unambiguous definition of the committed throughput metric (Committed Throughput Units, CTU) and measurement windows (5-min rolling for real-time thresholds, 30-day weighted for monthly entitlement).
An error-budget calculation that can be computed from existing telemetry (per-customer tokens/sec and successful response rate) and a worked example with numbers.
Draft contract language (two variants: 'standard' and 'SLAs-with-autoscale') vetted by Legal and Sales and approved for use in negotiation.
Operational controls and autoscale policy constraints documented (ramp rates, minimum headroom, queueing behavior, fallback models) and linked to engineering implementation tickets.
A remediation playbook that maps severity (quantile breach levels) to customer-facing notifications, credits computation, and forced mitigation steps (e.g., fleet cordon/priority migration).
Sign-off from Reliability (SRE), Runtime, and Legal as captured in comment threads or approval checkboxes.
decisions: Adopt CTU (Committed Throughput Unit) measured in tokens-per-second aligned to request billing to keep measurement meaningful for customers with varied prompt lengths.
Use a dual-window approach: 5-minute rolling quantile for operational SLO triggers and a 30-day weighted availability window for contractual credit calculations.
Service credit cap: 100% of the monthly Dedicated fee for catastrophic multi-AZ failovers; tiered credit bands for partial degradation (see Credit Matrix below).
Autoscale interplay: allow autoscaler to trigger burst capacity for up to 10% of committed baseline without triggering crediting, but require headroom reservation of at least 5% for burst protection.
implementation_notes: Telemetry: Add CTU time-series (tokens/sec per customer per model) to metrics-store with 1s granularity and precomputed 5-min and 30-day aggregates. Engineering ticket ENG-812345 created for instrumentation.
Billing integration: Ensure tokens/sec aggregates used for CTU align with billing counters to avoid disputes; Finance and Billing OWN-PR-77 coordinating mapping.

Autoscaler constraints: Runtime to expose policy knobs: min_reserve_fraction, ramp_rate_tokens_per_min, burst_allowance_pct. Proposed defaults: min_reserve_fraction=0.05, ramp_rate=500k tokens/min, burst_allowance_pct=0.10.
Fleet controls: implement 'cordon' API (runtime endpoint) that sets node priorities for customer slices and a graceful evict policy to move non-critical workloads first. ENG-814999 tracks api work.
Testing: Create synthetic workload harness to replay customer traffic patterns and validate credit computation. Add regression test to CI.
credit_matrix: Monthly entitlement = committed CTU * 30 days (weighted by peak profile).
If monthly delivered CTU >= 99.5% of entitlement -> no credit.
If monthly delivered CTU between 98% and 99.5% -> 10% service credit of monthly Dedicated fee.
If monthly delivered CTU between 95% and 98% -> 30% service credit.
If monthly delivered CTU < 95% -> 60% service credit, up to 100% in case of verified catastrophic multi-AZ outage.
Credits are pro-rated per incident window and capped as defined in the contract annex.
error_budget_formula: Compute per-customer CTU timeseries T(t) sampled at 1s; define committed CTU as C (tokens/sec).
Operational breach if P95(T over 5min) < 0.9 * C (can be tuned per tier).
Monthly delivered fraction F = (sum_t min(T(t), C) * dt) / (C * number_of_seconds_in_period).
Service credit band determined by Error budget consumed mapped to Credit Matrix. Example worked numbers included in appendix.
contract_clauses: Sample clause - Measurement: 'Committed Throughput Units (CTU) shall be measured as customer-specific, model-agnostic tokens-per-second using Redwood's billing tokenization policy. The Provider will compute 5-minute rolling aggregates and a 30-day weighted delivered fraction for the purpose of SLO evaluation and crediting.'

Sample clause - Notification: 'Provider will notify Customer within 60 minutes of detecting an operational breach of the 5-minute quantile threshold and provide remediation ETA. Customer must report suspected measurement disputes within 14 days of the monthly invoice.'

Sample clause - Credits: 'If the monthly delivered fraction falls below stated bands, Provider will issue a service credit per the Credit Matrix. Credits are applied to the next invoice and are Customer's sole remedy for throughput degradations under this Agreement.'

Sample clause - Autoscale and Headroom: 'Provider may use autoscale burst capacity up to the contracted burst allowance without crediting. Provider will maintain minimum reserved headroom of 5% of committed CTU unless explicitly waived via written amendment.'
Sample clause - Limitations: 'Credits do not apply to degradations caused by Customer misconfiguration, force majeure, or maintenance notices provided 72 hours in advance.'
operational_playbook: Detection: Alert if 5-min rolling P95 < 0.9*C for two consecutive 5-min windows -> page SRE and assigned account SE.

Triage: Run 'priority tranche check' to identify whether degradation is localized (single AZ, model shard) or systemic. Use fleet tracing to map to nodes. ENG-820001 will add tracing tag support per-customer.
Mitigation: If localized, cordon affected nodes and shift traffic to standby pool; if systemic, enable burst_pool up to 20% while autoscale provisions reserved nodes.

Remediation: Post-incident, compute delivered fraction and reconcile against Credit Matrix; draft customer-facing postmortem and remediation timeline. Legal must approve credit calculations before issuance.
